translations.help.title: CaptionForge help
translations.help.heading: A quick guide to your subtitles
translations.help.summary: CaptionForge transcribes the clips you select and applies the formatting of an existing template in your CapCut project.
translations.help.projects.title: 1. Project and timeline
translations.help.projects.body: Find your CapCut projects folder and select a project. Then choose the timeline by its name and cover. CapCut's pinned timeline is not changed. If the selected timeline is pinned, the root draft and its .bak are also updated; otherwise, those root files are preserved.
translations.help.audio.title: 2. Clips and media
translations.help.audio.body: First choose the source track by name. If CapCut has not named it, a file name from that track is shown. Audio or Video appears separately and reflects the CapCut track type. Then select the clips on that track to transcribe. Each clip retains its trimming, position and timeline gaps. Other tracks are excluded from this generation. Include all and Exclude all affect only the visible track. Excluding does not delete files. If you edited the project in CapCut, save it and click Refresh: tracks and templates are reloaded while preserving selections for clips that still exist. Refresh discards the previously prepared result. The ▶ button plays the trimmed clip; use Locate if you moved or renamed a file.
translations.help.template.title: 3. Template and Whisper
translations.help.template.body: In CapCut, add a subtitle with the template and formatting you want, save, and click Refresh in CaptionForge. Select that template track. Its font, colors, position and animation become the template. Choose the GGML model, transcription language and CPU threads; the interface language is configured separately.
translations.help.generate.title: 4. Generate and review
translations.help.generate.body: Click Generate subtitles. The audio will be prepared and transcribed by Whisper. Progress counts completed clips; a long clip may take longer without moving the progress bar. Review all result blocks and timings. You can export the complete text to SRT before applying it.
translations.help.apply.title: 5. Apply and overwrite
translations.help.apply.body: Close CapCut before applying. Only subtitles on the selected template track are replaced; other tracks are preserved. A recognized sample template is replaced directly. If the track contains edited or generated text, confirmation is requested. Canceling that confirmation preserves the prepared result and leaves the project unchanged.
translations.help.backups.title: 6. Backups and restoration
translations.help.backups.body: Before writing, CaptionForge backs up affected files and synchronizes CapCut's .bak files. View runs under Backups for this timeline and restore one with CapCut closed. Restoration checks that files have not changed since that run. Do not force restoration if the project has been edited since then.
translations.help.settings.title: 7. Settings and languages
translations.help.settings.body: The gear opens preferences from any screen. Theme, palette and interface language apply immediately. Workspace and tool paths are saved on confirmation. To add a language, copy es.json, translate its values, change code and name, and save it under its two-letter code. Opening the language list rescans Languages; missing translations fall back to Spanish.
translations.help.diagnostics.title: 8. Diagnostics
translations.help.diagnostics.body: If an operation fails, check its message and the clip and tool paths. Detailed CapCut, Whisper, FFmpeg and Windows messages are preserved as original diagnostics. Logs are in %LOCALAPPDATA%\CaptionForge\Logs. The tutorial explains controls and never automatically runs transcription, application or restoration operations.
translations.tutorial.title: CaptionForge tutorial
translations.tutorial.offer: Would you like a tour of CaptionForge's main controls? You can skip it and start it again from Help.
translations.tutorial.busy: Wait for the operation to finish. You can skip the tutorial at any time.
translations.tutorial.targetPending: This control will be available on its corresponding screen.
translations.tutorial.requirement.SupportedTemplate: Select a supported template to continue.
translations.tutorial.requirement.Result: Generate subtitles and wait for the result to continue.
translations.tutorial.projects.folder.title: Find your projects
translations.tutorial.projects.folder.body: The usual CapCut folder is detected at startup. Use Browse folder if your projects are elsewhere, and Refresh to read them again.
translations.tutorial.projects.choose.title: Select the project
translations.tutorial.projects.choose.body: Choose a card. Covers retain their video aspect ratio. You can filter by name. After selecting a project, Next takes you to its timelines.
translations.tutorial.timelines.choose.title: Choose the timeline
translations.tutorial.timelines.choose.body: Select where to create subtitles. Pinned indicates the timeline CapCut uses at the project root; choosing another does not move that pin.
translations.tutorial.audio.clips.title: Include only the clips you need
translations.tutorial.audio.clips.body: Select clips from the source track to transcribe. Include all and Exclude all affect only this track. Trimming and timeline gaps are preserved; excluding a clip does not remove it from the project.
translations.tutorial.audio.preview.title: Listen to each trimmed clip
translations.tutorial.audio.preview.body: Choosing a track prepares its first playable clip without starting playback. Click Play on the bar to listen. The title shows the clip number and file, and the loaded row is highlighted. Clicking ▶ on another clip loads that trimmed clip. Pause preserves the position, and Stop returns to the beginning; you can then play it again.
translations.tutorial.template.choose.title: Choose the template track
translations.tutorial.template.choose.body: Select the template you prepared in CapCut. Generation preserves its appearance and animation. Applying replaces that track; other tracks are preserved.
translations.tutorial.whisper.options.title: Configure transcription
translations.tutorial.whisper.options.body: Choose a GGML model, audio language and CPU threads. The recommendation leaves some CPU capacity available. Whisper's language is independent of this interface language.
translations.tutorial.captions.generate.title: Generate subtitles
translations.tutorial.captions.generate.body: Click Generate subtitles after selecting clips, template and model. The process prepares the audio and transcribes its words; this tutorial does not click that button for you.
translations.tutorial.captions.review.title: Review the complete result
translations.tutorial.captions.review.body: Check the blocks, their timeline timings and their text. You can scroll through the entire list and export a complete SRT before changing CapCut.
translations.tutorial.captions.apply.title: Apply to the selected track
translations.tutorial.captions.apply.body: Close CapCut and click Apply when you are satisfied with the result. A backup is saved. If edited subtitles already exist, confirmation is requested; you can cancel and preserve the result.
translations.tutorial.backups.restore.title: Return to the previous state
translations.tutorial.backups.restore.body: Expand Backups for this timeline, choose a run, and restore with CapCut closed. Change detection protects later edits. You do not need to restore anything to advance through this tutorial.
translations.tutorial.settings.open.title: Preferences within reach
translations.tutorial.settings.open.body: The gear opens theme, palette, interface language and paths. Help lets you repeat this tour or see new steps as features are added. Completed steps are saved.
